question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**William Jones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sir William Jones, a British philologist and orientalist, founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784.
 
• The establishment aimed to promote Oriental studies, including the study of Indian languages, literature, and culture.
 
• The society was created in Calcutta (now Kolkata), which was then the capital of British India.
 
• William Jones is renowned for his work in comparative linguistics and for proposing the existence of a relationship among European and Indian languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asiatic Society of Bengal:**

 
 
• The society's official name at its inception was "Asiatick Society."
 
• It played a pivotal role in the development of Indology and the study of Asian cultures and histories.
 
• The society published a journal called "Asiatic Researches," which disseminated knowledge about Asian civilizations.
 
• Over time, the Asiatic Society contributed significantly to the preservation and dissemination of ancient Indian manuscripts and texts.
 
 
 
• **William Jones:**
 
 
• He was born on September 28, 1746, and died on April 27, 1794.
 
• Jones was a pioneer in the study of Sanskrit and is known for his translations of ancient Indian texts.
 
• He proposed the existence of a Proto-Indo-European language, showing connections between Latin, Greek, and Sanskrit.
 
• His work laid the foundation for modern comparative linguistics.
 
 
 
• **Indology:**
 
 
• Indology is the academic study of the history, cultures, languages, and literature of India and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Indologists study ancient texts, inscriptions, and other historical materials to understand India's past.
 
• The field encompasses various disciplines, including archaeology, history, and philology.
 
• Prominent Indologists include Max Müller, A.L. Basham, and R.G. Bhandarkar.
